key_insight: Solution-phase ligand exchange enables thicker AgBiS2 nanocrystal absorbers for near-infrared harvesting, supporting experimentally demonstrated 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems.
engineering_relevance: Improved charge extraction in thicker AgBiS2 films offers a scalable route to stable near-infrared sub-cells paired with visible-light-absorbing perovskites.
method: Model tandem performance using the experimental AgBiS2 absorption spectrum.
Use solution-phase ligand exchange for one-step deposition of passivated, thicker nanocrystal films.
Integrate AgBiS2 with lead-halide perovskites in four-terminal and monolithic tandems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 24.0% four-terminal tandem efficiency, voltage addition in monolithic tandems, and >90% efficiency retention after three months in dry air without encapsulation; triple-junction efficiencies above 47.9% are modeled, not demonstrated.
watch_item: Practical tandem performance still depends on charge transport and optical integration; dry-air storage stability does not establish durability under continuous operation.
paper_title: Stable AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
